newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Sakhalin-II gives Russian firm oil platform deal.
newsitem.headline: Sakhalin-II gives Russian firm oil platform deal.

text.p: One of Russia's largest foreign oil consortiums came one step closer to the production stage on Friday when it awarded a $35 million contract to a Russian shipbuilder for a platform for its offshore project.

Sakhalin Energy Investment Company Ltd said in a statement that the contract, to the Amur Shipbuilding Plant, was for a structure that will be converted into a drilling and production platform in 1998 for its approximately $10 billion Sakhalin-II project off the Far Eastern Island of Sakhalin.
But Sakhalin Energy President Frank Duffield said the group's production-sharing contract depended on Russia passing adequate oil and gas laws, which Moscow has promised to do.

Sakhalin Energy, which signed its contract with the Russian government in June 1994, is the operating arm of the MMMSM consortium grouping units of Marathon, McDermott, Mitsui & Co Ltd, Royal Dutch/Shell and Mitsubishi Corp subsidiary Diamond Gas Sakhalin BV.
The platform will initially serve as a support base for an existing mobile drilling unit, but will function as a platform when the consortium begins drilling for production oil in 1999.

If Sakhalin Energy sticks to its schedule, it will be the first consortium to produce significant amounts of oil off Russia's Sahkalin coast, where two other foreign consortiums also have multi-billion dollar projects.
The platform is for the Piltun-Astokhskoye (PA) field, one of two the consortium plans to develop.

The two fields, on Sakhalin's continental shelf in the Sea of Okhotsk, hold estimated recoverable oil reserves of 100 million tonnes (about 750 million barrels), as well as nearly 500 billion cubic metres (14 trillion cubic feet) of gas.
